card.name: Nongkrem
card.tagline: Five-day Khasi thanksgiving dance for harvest and prosperity
card.profile: Ka Pomblang Nongkrem, popularly the Nongkrem dance, is a five-day Khasi religious festival held in autumn at Smit, headquarters of the Syiem (chief) of Hima Khyrim, about 11 km from Shillong (Government of Meghalaya). It is performed to appease the goddess Ka Blei Synshar for a bumper harvest and the prosperity of the people; the Syiem of Khyrim and the high priest conduct the Pomblang ceremony, which includes the sacrifice of goats and offering of a cock to Lei Shyllong, the god of Shillong peak (Government of Meghalaya). Unmarried maidens in fine costumes dance in an inner circle (Ka Shad Kynthei) while men dance more vigorously around them (Ka Shad Mastieh), holding a sword in the right hand and a white yak-hair whisk in the left, to the beat of drums and tangmuri pipes (Government of Meghalaya; HONEI).
card.insight: The dances take place inside the Iing Sad, a large nail-free palace of bamboo and thatch; as a living religious ceremony rather than a tourist show, visitors are asked to remain silent and stay outside the defined ritual space (Meghalaya Cabs; Government of Meghalaya).
aliases: Ka Shad Kynthei / Ka Shad Mastieh
card.image_significance: Royal goat-sacrifice thanksgiving dance. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Meghalaya (Khasi), India.
